messages.content: Use web search to find relevant datasets. Only include landing pages or DOIs. Do not invent links. Do not call time, date, timestamp, or clock tools.

Query: Can you find datasets about protest movement, agricultural policy, and nutrition policy in Germany and Berlin during the 2020s, matching this research need: Survey data on Germany’s food justice movement, especially participants in the annual Berlin agrifood protest, covering socio-demographics, protest motivations, justice demands, political practices, and food-related practices, with comparable protest surveys from 2020 and 2024.
Respond ONLY as JSON in this exact shape: {"items":[{"title":"...","url_or_doi":"...","justification":"..."}]}. Put any DOI, URL, landing page, or link in url_or_doi.

queries: dataset protest survey Wir haben es satt 2020 2024 Berlin food justice movement sociodemographics motivations
2024 2020 Wir haben es satt protest survey dataset Germany food justice DOI
action.query: dataset protest survey Wir haben es satt 2020 2024 Berlin food justice movement sociodemographics motivations

content.text: {"items":[{"title":"Food for Justice: Power, Politics, and Food Inequalities in a Bioeconomy – Protest Surveys, Berlin, 2020 and 2024","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.7802/2783","justification":"Best match for the research need. This dataset, published through GESIS by the Food for Justice research project, investigates food justice movements and agrifood protests in Germany, particularly the annual 'Wir haben es satt!' demonstrations in Berlin in 2020 and 2024. It covers participants' sociodemographic characteristics, protest motivations, political attitudes and practices, demands for agricultural and food-system justice, and food-related behaviors. Topics include household food consumption, food production and self-cultivation, and food waste management. The research combines in-person interviews and online surveys, supporting comparisons between the 2020 and 2024 protest participants. The dataset's embargo ended on July 1, 2026, making it especially relevant for current research."},{"title":"Befragung 'Wir haben es satt!' 2020 – Berlin Protest Survey","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.7802/2802","justification":"Directly relevant survey dataset covering participants in the 'Wir haben es satt!' demonstration held in Berlin on January 18, 2020. Conducted by researchers from Freie Universität Berlin in cooperation with the Institute for Protest and Social Movement Research, the survey examines participants' demographic backgrounds, political orientations, mobilization pathways, protest motivations, organizational involvement, and attitudes toward sustainable agriculture and fair food production. It also investigates ethical consumption and food-related lifestyle practices. Provides a valuable 2020 baseline for comparison with the 2024 protest survey and for investigating changes in Germany's food justice movement."},{"title":"Food for Justice: Power, Politics, and Food Inequalities in a Bioeconomy (Berlin, 2020) – B2FIND Dataset Record","url_or_doi":"https://b2find.eudat.eu/dataset/b7c95ac2-b3c7-5daa-aa7a-7309a4e17b69","justification":"Research dataset discovery record documenting the Food for Justice investigation of Germany's agrifood movements, specifically the 'Wir haben es satt!' protest in Berlin. The project conducted protest surveys in 2020 and 2024 to investigate activists' characteristics, political engagement, food-system demands, and agricultural and nutritional practices. Particularly useful as an additional metadata discovery route for locating the relevant research data and understanding its geographical and temporal coverage. This is a discovery record rather than an independent survey dataset."},{"title":"Food for Justice – GESIS Research Data Record for Protest Surveys 2020 and 2024","url_or_doi":"https://search.gesis.org/research_data/SDN-10.7802-2783","justification":"Official GESIS dataset landing page linked by the Food for Justice research team. The dataset addresses social movements mobilizing against food inequalities, with particular emphasis on the Berlin 'Wir haben es satt!' protests in 2020 and 2024. It includes information on protesters' motivations, justice demands, sociodemographics, political activities, and food-related practices, including food preparation, household consumption, self-production, and waste management. This is the most relevant institutional access point for obtaining data and documentation supporting comparative analysis of the two protest years. It refers to the same dataset as the first entry."},{"title":"Farmers' Voices in European Protests: Diverse Complaints, Emotional Tones, and Policy Responses","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17435985","justification":"Complementary dataset covering the 2024 farmers' protests in Germany, France, Belgium, and the Netherlands. It contains coded information derived from 2,232 open-ended survey responses concerning farmers' motivations for protesting, agricultural policy grievances, emotional expressions, and policy responses at national and European levels. Relevant for contextualizing the German agricultural policy conflicts of 2024 and comparing farmers' demands with those of food justice activists participating in Berlin's 'Wir haben es satt!' demonstration. However, it does not specifically survey the Berlin food justice movement, does not provide a 2020 comparison, and does not include the original open-ended responses."}]}
